analysis:
All three changed files are test-only: AdmissionRateEstimatorTests.swift (added), EngineMeasurementOrderingTests.swift (added) and LaunchAgentRestartTests.swift (a new test inserted at about lines 181-204). No production source is in this batch, so no runtime behavior changes here.

The tests cover deadline-admission estimator behavior: the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES kill switch, stale-evidence fail-open, decode-shape plumbing, and out-of-order observation freshness. The behaviors are availability and performance-admission logic that affects TTFT deadline rejection. The nearest threat entries are the availability ones (T-010, T-029). None of A-001 through A-017 or TB-002, TB-003, TB-007 or TB-011 are touched in a way that regresses a control.

LaunchAgentRestartTests asserts that the new env key is in LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys, is not in WatchdogAgent.passthroughEnvKeys, and that unrelated env vars such as UNRELATED_SECRET are excluded from the plist. This reinforces the allowlist behavior.

Remaining question for integration: the production implementations are outside this batch (DeadlineAdmissionFixes, IsolatedPrefillAdmissionRate, EnginePerformanceMeasurements, the EngineV2Bridge changes, and the LaunchAgent passthrough list). They should be reviewed. Stale-evidence fail-open and the use of the anchor on an idle engine alter admission decisions. These could affect provider availability or load acceptance, but not confidentiality or attestation, based on these tests. No findings are raised on test-only evidence.
